clue.text: Voyager's visit is to a Jupiter satellite

parts.note: a traveller's visit or stop at a port is a call

explanation.surface: The Voyager space probe makes a fly-by of one of Jupiter's moons.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the NASA Voyager probe, but 'Voyager's visit' is simply a call, as a ship calls at a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the four large Galilean moons orbiting the planet Jupiter.

clue.text: They clash with the emblems, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of a word, not its spelling, so the emblems word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: emblems are symbols

explanation.surface: Things that conflict with heraldic badges, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymbals are brass percussion plates that are struck or clashed together.

clue.text: Measure of an extended ruling of the courts?

definitions.text: Measure of an extended ruling of the courts?

parts.words: Measure of an extended ruling of the courts?
parts.note: read as a long line chalked on a games court, a measure that also figures in the idiom for a big margin

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to gauge a lengthy judgment from the law courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling' and 'courts' suggest judges, but the ruling is a drawn line on a sports court, made in chalk; 'by a long chalk' is the British idiom for 'by a wide margin'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'by a long chalk' uses the phrase as a measure of great distance or difference.

clue.text: This month everything is put in place

parts.note: inst. (instant) is the old commercial abbreviation for this month
everything means all

explanation.surface: A notice that this month every item is being fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, short for 'instant', means 'of the current month' in old business letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To install equipment is to set it up in position, ready for use.

clue.text: Get up and produce, or go on strike

definitions.meaning: an outfit or getup is a ..., how someone is dressed
workers who strike ..., walking off the job

explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is an outfit or an output, and to turn out is to down tools, each a separate sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Very noisy in the tall building? Nonsense!

indicators.note: in places the very noisy letters inside the building word

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
ff (fortissimo) is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that a high-rise could be so loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish or twaddle.

clue.text: Irishman has a try in a changed situation in S America

parts.note: Pat (Patrick) is the stock crossword Irishman
to have a go is to have a try

indicators.note: changed tells us the two short words in and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irishman makes an attempt in different circumstances in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges IN A into NIA, which ends the answer after PAT, A and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonia is the region at the southern tip of South America, shared by Argentina and Chile.

clue.text: Cutter comes out of the Far West

indicators.note: a new word emerging out of the letters of Far West signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A bandit or cutthroat emerges from the American frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes out of' rearranges the seven letters of FAR WEST; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw for cutting intricate shapes in wood, so a cutting tool.

clue.text: Union trouble arising over one issue

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means reading the trouble word upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble
I is the Roman numeral one
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: A trade union dispute flares up over a single matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns AIL upward to LIA; 'over' places it above I and SON in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a close connection or relationship, a union of two parties.

clue.text: Writing introductions to Modern Science

definitions.meaning: the opening letters of these two words are M and S, the standard abbreviation for a handwritten document

explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten document is writing, and its usual abbreviation is MS, the initials of Modern Science.

clue.text: They half like young Hawk

indicators.note: half here takes the back half of the word They

parts.note: like means as

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain group partly resembles a youthful hawk.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyas is a nestling hawk, especially one taken for training in falconry.

clue.text: They get a sight or a close involvement in human antiquities

definitions.text: They get a sight or a close involvement in human antiquities

indicators.note: involvement suggests letters tangled together, so these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Diggers get to see and handle the relics of humanity's past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' rearranges the fourteen letters of A SIGHT OR A CLOSE, and the whole clue describes the people concerned.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeologists study human antiquity by excavating and examining ancient remains.

clue.text: In which the great detective had a study

definitions.text: In which the great detective had a study

parts.words: In which the great detective had a study
parts.note: a study here is the title of a Sherlock Holmes novel, not a room, and the colour names its setting

explanation.surface: Asks which place the famous sleuth used as his study.
explanation.walkthrough: A study sounds like Holmes's room, but it is Conan Doyle's first Holmes novel, 'A Study in Scarlet'.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Sherlock Holmes story is titled A Study in Scarlet, a vivid red.

clue.text: Vanish like actors at end of tempestuous revels

definitions.text: Vanish like actors at end of tempestuous revels

parts.words: Vanish like actors at end of tempestuous revels
parts.note: recalls Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest, saying the actors of his revels melted into air and thin air

explanation.surface: Disappear as the players do when a wild party ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tempestuous' points to The Tempest, where Prospero says 'Our revels now are ended. These our actors... are melted into air'.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to turn to vapour and disappear, as Prospero's spirit actors melt into thin air.

clue.text: Fly the ruler out about this time

indicators.note: the ruler word is spread out about the time word, enclosing it

parts.note: a king is a ruler
now means at this time

explanation.surface: An order to send the monarch away around now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb or insect; here it is slang for sharp or wide awake.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is British slang for shrewd and alert, as is a knowing person.

clue.text: One river Tristan diverted, annoying agents

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: a river diverted changes course, so the letters of Tristan are rearranged

explanation.surface: A river named Tristan has had its course altered, a nuisance to locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges TRISTAN into RITANTS, after I and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritants are things that cause annoyance or inflammation.

clue.text: Advance, or allow others to do so

definitions.meaning: to stand aside so others can pass

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to go forward and to step aside for others, two senses of clearing a path.

clue.text: Grow together on an island, say

indicators.note: say tells us the island phrase is pronounced rather than spelled

parts.note: an gives A and Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Things bond as one while on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals the sound: 'a Crete' is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by accumulating and fusing together.

clue.text: In the course of a soldiers' training march?

definitions.text: In the course of a soldiers' training march?

parts.words: In the course of a soldiers' training march?
parts.note: a soldiers' training walk is a route march, so being in the course of one is being on that route

explanation.surface: Asks what happens during an army training hike.
explanation.walkthrough: A route march is a long military training march; the answer means 'on the way'.
explanation.definitionFit: En route means on the way, in transit along a course.

clue.text: Reed provides material for an ancient 8

definitions.meaning: a tall aquatic sedge of the Nile
8 refers to 8-across, a handwritten text; the ancient writing material was made from the pith of the reed

explanation.surface: A reed supplies stuff for an old handwritten document.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus is the Nile sedge and the paper-like writing sheets the Egyptians made from it.

clue.text: Boss of this area over mine?

definitions.text: Boss of this area over mine?

parts.words: Boss of this area over mine?
parts.note: a boss is a head, and the area at the top of a coal mine shaft combines the mine word with that head

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is in charge of the patch above their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a manager senior to 'mine'; actually the head (boss) of a pit (mine) is the surface area at the top of the shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: The pithead is the top of a mineshaft and the buildings around it.

clue.text: Stipulation for five is nothing

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
V is the Roman numeral five
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rule decreeing that five equals zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A proviso is a condition attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Maud was "tall and stately" — and only this it would seem

definitions.text: Maud was "tall and stately" — and only this it would seem

parts.words: Maud was "tall and stately" — and only this it would seem
parts.note: recalls Tennyson's poem Maud, where the girl is not seventeen but is tall and stately, so her age is one less

explanation.surface: Maud looked tall and dignified, though apparently she was only so old.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's Maud has 'Maud is not seventeen, But she is tall and stately', so she must be younger than seventeen.
explanation.definitionFit: One year short of seventeen is the age implied for Tennyson's heroine.

clue.text: The fat man's financial burden?

parts.note: a corporation is old slang for a pot belly, so a levy on that paunch is the business tax

explanation.surface: Asks what weighs on a stout man's wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is dated British slang for a large belly; corporation tax is the UK tax on company profits.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation tax is the levy on company profits, read jokily as a tax on a paunch.

clue.text: He has two sound associations with bells

definitions.text: He has two sound associations with bells

parts.words: He has two sound associations with bells
parts.note: the man's title sounds like Bow, of the London Bow Bells, and he is the partner of a belle

explanation.surface: A man linked twice over with ringing bells.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow Bells ring in the City of London; the answer is pronounced like 'Bow', and a gentleman admirer is paired with a 'belle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or male admirer, the traditional companion of a belle.

clue.text: Faithfulness for example in marriage

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for example inside the marriage word

parts.note: a marriage is an alliance

explanation.surface: Loyalty, as shown within wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is loyalty or fidelity owed to a sovereign or cause.

clue.text: All this is as it should be

definitions.text: All this is as it should be

parts.words: All this is as it should be
parts.note: the phrase all ... is old British slang for everything being fine

explanation.surface: A reassurance that everything is in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All serene' is a dated British expression meaning all is well; put the answer after 'All' to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means calm and untroubled, as in the expression that all is well.

clue.text: With repaired van, Woods provides right to a living

indicators.note: repaired suggests the van and Woods are taken apart and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Woods, his van fixed, provides a means of earning his keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges VAN and WOODS; 'living' is a church benefice, not an income.
explanation.definitionFit: An advowson is the right to appoint a clergyman to a parish benefice in the Church of England.
